title: Dropping the ruler vs. holding it still
caption: One first frame, two instructions. Top (A, the real event): a hand drops the ruler onto the notebook. Bottom (B): the hand holds the ruler above the notebook and nothing moves. The untrained Wan2.2 does the same thing for both: it slides the ruler to the right edge of the notebook and holds it there. MoPlan puts the ruler down on the notebook for A, as in the real video, and keeps it where it is for B.
benchmark_detail: first frame of Something-Something v2 validation video 9578 with an instruction pair from data/moprobe/moprobe_h_rows.jsonl; this frame was removed from MoProbe-H by the item check (data/moprobe/rejected_frames.json), so it is not part of the MoProbe-H set or its measurements

protocol.name: moprobe
protocol.image: RGB, resized to 448x256 with LANCZOS (stretched, no crop). The input PNG is the source frame letterboxed onto a 1280x720 (16:9) canvas.

sampler.scheduler: UniPCMultistepScheduler of the Wan2.2 pipeline (flow shift 3.0)
sampler.guidance_note: the same scale is used for the high-noise and the low-noise expert

protocol.output: uint8 frames [37, 256, 448, 3]; the reference hashes are of these frames saved with numpy.save

seed_rule: seed = 42 + (crc32(sample_id) mod 100000), seed index 0; both models use the same seed; the noise comes from torch.Generator('cuda').manual_seed(seed)
